summary: chainLoadGate declares it reads a batch — the last builtin withholding it, over four facts a batch states in full
acceptance: `chainLoadGate` is a `BatchingGate` whose `run` takes the context union, so a phase whose `afterMerge` gates are builtins reaches the width it declared with chain-load among them; both shipped statements move with it — the roster bullet and the *Reading a batched merge* sentence that today gives the withholding a reason the gate's own reads contradict; and the narrowing arm keeps a subject that genuinely withholds rather than losing the case
tests: chainLoadGate declares it reads a batch
a phase whose afterMerge gates are builtins reaches the declared merge width with chain-load among them
pins: a chain-authored gate that withholds the batch declaration holds its phase to one span per merge

interface.changes: `chainLoadGate` is a `BatchingGate`, so a chain may hang it at `afterMerge` on a batching phase without collapsing the phase to one span per merge
interface.hides: which gate point costs width — an author no longer reads a builtin's own field set to learn whether placing it at the merge narrows the wave
interface.rejected: leaving it a `SingleSpanGate` and stating the cost in prose: the withholding's stated reason is false on the tree, so the prose would stand in for a declaration the gate can carry

notes: Measured here: the gate reads `ctx.touchedPaths`, `repoRoot`, `configDir`, `flumeDir` and nothing else (`src/builtinGates.ts:262`) — the last three are `GateSite`, and `touchedPaths` is the spans' union, the right subject asked once. `writablePathsGate` is `afterCommit` and per-span, so this is the last builtin hangable at the merge. The `docs/` reason and `tests/gateBatch.test.ts:159`'s comment are the sentence that was wrong about `pendingGate` (ff9ecef7).
